recentItems.title: How AI and social media are destroying the internet | Jake Renzella | TEDxUNSW
recentItems.description:
Dr Jake Renzella reveals how AI-driven misinformation campaigns shape our digital landscape, from nation-states to special-interest groups manipulating elections and narratives. Discover why social media platforms profit from bot activity and what you can do to reclaim truth. 

Dr Jake Renzella. Senior Lecturer in CSE at UNSW, Co-Head of the Computing and Education research group, and Director of Studies in Computer Science, Dr Renzella has a lot to offer when it comes to computers, AI, and education. 

Much of his research focuses on the fields of Pedagogical Generative AI and education technology. He has also built complex open source education technologies & is passionate about aligning AI technology with current Australian curriculums. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What they didn't teach you in school | Samantha Kaye | TEDxCrawley
recentItems.description:
English, Math(s), Science....  yes personal finance.... no Samantha Kaye guides us through the mine field of personal finance, certainly something that has never been taught in school! Samantha Kaye is a Chartered Financial Adviser and Fellow of the Personal Finance Society. Passionate about financial education, she helps individuals and families make informed decisions that create confidence, security and long-term wellbeing.

Through her work, Samantha champions practical life skills and financial literacy, believing that everyone deserves access to the knowledge needed to make better decisions for their future. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What We Miss When We Only See Poverty | Benjamin John | TEDxJimeta
recentItems.description:
When we look at vulnerable communities or regions like Northeast Nigeria, what do we usually see? Headlines often reduce people to their suffering—hunger, displacement, poverty, and a lack of resources.

In this moving TEDx talk, Dr. Benjamin John shares a transformative encounter with a malnourished child in Dikwa in 2018 that reshaped their understanding of aid and development. Challenging the habit of viewing communities merely as passive recipients of charity, the talk reveals how vulnerability does not erase capability, resilience, or local knowledge.

Discover why lasting change requires shifting our mindset from "What can we do for this community?" to "What can we build with them?"—fostering true partnership, ownership, and sustainable impact. Benjamin John is a development and humanitarian professional focused on improving the lives of vulnerable and crisis-affected communities, particularly in Northeast Nigeria.

His work spans education, protection, livelihoods, health, peacebuilding, and community development.

As Executive Director of Unique Care and Support Foundation (CASFOD) and a member of the Malala Fund's Education Championship Network, he promotes local ownership, innovation, and collaboration to build resilient communities and create sustainable opportunities. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Development In Real Estate | Sanju Thakran | TEDxSGU
recentItems.description:
In this inspiring TEDx Talk, Sanju Thakran, Founder and Director of Thakur Logistic Park, shares his remarkable journey of entering the logistics and real estate industry at just 22, despite having no prior experience or family business background in the sector. After facing startup failures during COVID-19, he returned to India with a clear vision, overcame criticism and industry challenges, and worked towards building successful business projects through determination, continuous learning, and self-belief.
Through his journey, Sanju delivers a powerful message to young entrepreneurs and aspiring leaders: “Turn Your Problems into Fuel.” He highlights the importance of believing in yourself before others do, staying focused on your vision, and treating obstacles as opportunities for growth. His talk reminds us that success is not simply about luck, but about consistent effort, resilience, and the courage to pursue what others may consider impossible. Sanju Thakran is a real estate and logistics infrastructure professional and serves as the Director of Thakran Logistic Park (TLP), a warehousing and logistics development located near the KMP Expressway, Delhi-Mumbai Expressway and NH-48 in Haryana.
Through his leadership at Thakran Logistic Park, Sanju Thakran is associated with the development of modern warehousing infrastructure designed to support the evolving requirements of businesses and supply chains. TLP is being developed across an 85-acre land parcel, with its first phase planned to include approximately 5.22 lakh sq. ft. of development, including dedicated warehousing spaces designed for operational efficiency and scalability. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Oltre Al Jazeera: dal telegiornale al feed. Chi fa luce sul mondo? | Barbara Serra | TEDxSassari
recentItems.description:
Negli ultimi vent’anni Barbara Serra ha vissuto dall’interno una doppia rivoluzione del giornalismo. Nel 2006 è tra i giornalisti che lanciano Al Jazeera English, il canale che segna la fine del monopolio occidentale sull’informazione globale. Lo stesso anno Facebook si apre a tutti, dando il via all’era digitale dell’informazione. Se il motto di Al Jazeera era “la voce di chi non ha voce”, i social hanno dato voce a tutti. L’algoritmo sta sostituendo la scaletta del TG e i telespettatori sono diventati followers. Vent’anni dopo, Barbara Serra porta sul palco di TEDx Sassari una domanda fondamentale: siamo davvero meglio informati? Chi fa luce sul mondo? Giornalista, documentarista e scrittrice, Barbara Serra ha lavorato tra BBC, Al Jazeera English e Sky News UK, raccontando il mondo dall’Europa, dal Medio Oriente e da Washington. È stata la prima giornalista non madrelingua inglese a condurre un telegiornale in prima serata sulla televisione britannica.
Nel 2020 realizza Fascism in the Family, sulla storia di suo nonno, podestà di Carbonia: premiato ai New York Festivals TV & Film Awards, diventa nel 2025 il libro Fascismo in famiglia (Garzanti). This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What can I do? | Annisa Azkia Suryadi | TEDxCRIBS Youth
recentItems.description:
Imagine walking past a pile of coconut shells. What do you see? Most people would probably see waste. Now imagine seeing a river filled with dirty water. What do you see? A problem. But what if, instead of seeing them as two separate problems, we ask “Could one problem become part of the solution to another?” That was the question that changed the way I see the world.
 Azkia was born on 23 August 2011. Azkia is a Grade 10 student from Cahaya Rancamaya
who enjoys learning new things, especially science and environmental research. She is
interested in exploring new ideas, gaining different perspectives, and finding creative
solutions to real-world problems. Through her participation in TEDx, Azkia hopes to share
her ideas with others, inspire meaningful discussions, and encourage people to think beyond
the ordinary. She believes that even small ideas can grow into something meaningful and
make a positive impact on society. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Hours Behind the Seconds | Mr. Sapan Joshi | TEDxJGIS Youth
recentItems.description: Mentalist and illusionist Sapan Joshi takes us behind the seemingly impossible moments audiences witness on stage. Drawing on two decades of experience, he reveals the countless hours of practice, failure, observation and correction hidden behind a few effortless seconds. The talk reminds us that extraordinary achievement is rarely the result of talent alone—it is built through persistence, learning from mistakes and continuing even when we are not yet good. Sapan Joshi is a mentalist, illusionist and psychological entertainer with over 20 years of experience creating experiences that explore perception, psychology and the mysteries of the human mind. His performances blend psychology, observation and suggestion with sophisticated entertainment, inviting audiences to question how they perceive, decide and interpret reality. Over his career, Sapan has performed at 1,500+ events across 10+ countries, entertaining audiences in India and internationally. His work has also taken him to events for organisations and brands including Google, Microsoft, Mercedes-Benz, Samsung, Audi, BMW, Jio and the Adani Group. Rather than presenting his craft as supernatural, Sapan describes it as an interplay of psychological techniques and performance. Through interaction, curiosity and surprise, he creates memorable experiences that challenge assumptions and reveal how fascinating the human mind can be. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Why Not? The Question That Changes Everything | Dr. Sudipti Arora | TEDxJGIS Youth
recentItems.description: Through defining moments from her personal and professional journey, Dr. Sudipti Arora explores the power of asking, “Why not?” She shows how keeping possibility open can help us face uncertainty, challenge perceived limitations and take meaningful action. The talk is not about blind optimism, but about combining hope with effort, resilience and the willingness to try again. Dr. Sudipti Arora is an Environmental Research Scientist, sustainability leader and entrepreneur working at the intersection of science, climate action and societal impact. A PhD in Environmental Engineering from IIT Roorkee, she is Director–Research & Innovation at Dr. B. Lal Institute of Biotechnology and Founder-Director of Prakrit Sustainable Integrated Foundation and Prakrit Innovations. Her work spans water and wastewater management, circular economy, zero-waste and net-zero models, climate resilience and ESG. She has led nationally funded rural transformation initiatives, including the Aandhi Zero-Waste Village model, translating research into scalable community solutions. A Chevening CRISP Fellow at the University of Oxford, she is also Chairwoman, CII-IWN Rajasthan (2026–27). Her work is driven by one belief: science creates its greatest impact when it moves beyond laboratories to transform people, communities and systems. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Jack of All Trades, Master of Some | Mr. Abhinav Singh Kaurav | TEDxJGIS Youth
recentItems.description: In a world that often pressures people to specialise early, Abhinav Singh Kaurav presents a different possibility. Drawing from his experience across varied interests and disciplines, he explains how seemingly unrelated skills can strengthen one another. His talk encourages young people to explore widely, develop selected areas deeply and create an identity that is not limited to a single label. Abhinav Singh Kaurav is a singer-songwriter, composer, storyteller, writer, speaker, content creator and IT professional who blends creativity and technology. A Civil Engineering graduate, he works as a Lead Database Administrator while pursuing music and storytelling. He created “Abhi Ki Duniya,” a houseful musical storytelling show combining narrative theatre, original live music and visuals. His debut album, “Pehal,” features his original compositions. He has performed at several prestigious institutions and platforms, including TEDx events, college festivals, concerts and independent shows. Recognised as Young Achiever 2025, he has also opened for established artists. He has been featured on several prominent radio shows, including Akashwani, My FM, Red FM and more. His journey reflects the courage to pursue multiple passions and create an identity beyond conventional boundaries. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Between “I Don’t Know” and “Let Me Try” | Ms. Uma Oza | TEDxJGIS Youth
recentItems.description:
Courage does not always arrive before action. Sometimes it develops only after we take the first uncertain step. Drawing on her experiences in television and her decision to leave professional security to build something new, Uma Oza explores how responsible risk-taking, preparation and action can transform fear into confidence and personal growth. Uma Oza is a thought leader in education and human development with over four decades of experience transforming how individuals and institutions learn, lead and evolve. Her work integrates Nonviolent Communication into leadership and learning, fostering cultures rooted in trust, empathy and conscious responsibility. She has pursued advanced studies in Teaching for Understanding and Coaching for Understanding at Harvard University and is a certified facilitator of The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People and Theatre of the Oppressed. She also holds an international certification in Theme-Centred Interaction from the Ruth Cohn Institute, Berlin. Currently Vice President at the Competitiveness Mindset Institute, USA, Uma is also visiting faculty at IITGN-X, Institute of Design and Nirma University. Her work is anchored in nurturing conscious leaders and compassionate systems that move beyond performance to purpose and create meaningful, sustainable change.

recentItems.title: Beyond Bouncing Back: What Disasters Teach Us About Resilience | Dr. Prerna Singh | TEDxJGIS Youth
recentItems.description: Disasters test more than infrastructure—they reveal how people, institutions and communities respond when familiar systems collapse. Drawing from her experience in disaster resilience, Dr. Prerna Singh challenges the idea that resilience simply means returning to the way things were. She explains why meaningful recovery requires preparedness, adaptability, collaboration and the courage to build better pathways for the future. Dr. Prerna Singh is an infrastructure resilience and climate adaptation specialist whose work bridges research, policy and real-world implementation. With an academic background in Civil Engineering, including a PhD and MS from Georgia Institute of Technology and a BTech from IIT Gandhinagar, she has worked across academia, international development and resilience-focused organisations. Her professional journey includes work connected with UNDP, the Asian Disaster Preparedness Center and the Adaptation Research Alliance Infrastructure, along with leadership in climate-adaptation learning and research. Her expertise centres on strengthening infrastructure and communities against climate and disaster risks, locally led adaptation, systems thinking and long-term resilience. She is passionate about translating rigorous research into practical approaches that enable communities and institutions to navigate uncertainty and build more resilient futures. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Improving Is Not Always Becoming Perfect | Medina Nurianisa | TEDxCRIBS Youth
recentItems.description:
I think most of us want to be good at what we do. We want good results. We want people to be proud of us. And, sometimes, we want to be perfect. But I learned something when I failed: Trying to be perfect can stop us from growing. So, never be afraid of failure. Never be afraid of making mistakes, and don't wait until you are perfect before you try to make a difference. Start with yourself. Because sometimes, becoming a better version of yourself is the first step towards creating a better world.
 Medina is a 10-Grader at Cahaya Rancamaya Islamic Boarding School. She has reading comics, solving toy-puzzles such as LEGO, Gundams and listening to music as her hobbies. She wants to explain her feelings through speaking in public—to let everyone know that what she’s interested in aren’t only ordinary activities. By participating as a TEDx speaker, she hopes that one day she can actually speak up about her things. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
